p1.key: Mass = n × M: N2H4 1.0 × 32 = 32 g; N2 2.0 × 28 = 56 g; NH3 3.0 × 17 = 51 g; H2 25.0 × 2 = 50 g. The large number of moles of H2 is a distractor.
Divide each percentage by Ar: Mg 24/24 = 1, Si 28/28 = 1, O 48/16 = 3. The ratio 1 : 1 : 3 gives MgSiO3.
M(C3H7OH) = 60 g mol−1, so one molecule has mass 60 / 6.0 × 1023 = 1.0 × 10−22 g. 60 g is the mass of a whole mole.
C6H3(NO2)3 is C6H3N3O6. Dividing by the common factor 3 gives the simplest whole-number ratio C2HNO2. D is the molecular formula, and C is not written as an empirical formula.
n = cV = 0.2 mol dm−3 × 0.025 dm3 = 0.005 mol. Remember to convert 25 cm3 into dm3.
Empirical formulas: C6H6 → CH (13), C4H10 → C2H5 (29), C3H6 → CH2 (14), C2H6 → CH3 (15). C4H10 has the greatest.

The lower the H : C ratio, the higher the % carbon. C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>2</sub> (CH) is 24/26 = 92.3 % C, more than C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub> (85.7 %), C<sub>3</sub>H<sub>8</sub> (81.8 %) or C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub> (82.8 %).

The molar mass must be a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula mass. C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O = 44, and 2 × 44 = 88 (C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>8</sub>O<sub>2</sub>). 88 is not a multiple of CH<sub>2</sub> (14), CH<sub>2</sub>O (30) or CH<sub>3</sub>O (31).
n(S) = 3.2/32 = 0.10 mol; n(O) = 4.8/16 = 0.30 mol. Ratio S : O = 1 : 3, so the empirical formula is SO3.
Moles per 100 g: C 60/12 = 5.0, H 8/1 = 8.0, O 32/16 = 2.0. Ratio 5 : 8 : 2 gives C<sub>5</sub>H<sub>8</sub>O<sub>2</sub>, which can also be the molecular formula.
Moles of O atoms: A 0.3 × 4 = 1.2; B 0.6 × 3 = 1.8; C 0.7 × 2 = 1.4; D 0.8 × 1 = 0.8 mol, the smallest.

Ca<sup>2+</sup> and NO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup> are spectator ions. n(Ca<sup>2+</sup>) = 2.0 × 0.50 = 1.0 mol; n(NO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup>) = 1.0 × 2.0 = 2.0 mol; total volume 3.0 dm<sup>3</sup>. [Ca<sup>2+</sup>] = 0.33 and [NO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup>] = 0.67 mol dm<sup>−3</sup>.
n(H<sup>+</sup>) = cV: A 0.0100 × 0.250 = 0.00250 mol; B 0.00500; C 0.00500; D 0.00250 × 2 = 0.00500 (H<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> is diprotic). A has the least.

p1.key: Per 100 g: C 90/12 = 7.5 mol, H 10/1 = 10 mol. Ratio 7.5 : 10 = 3 : 4, so the empirical formula is C3H4.

p1.key: Each C2H5OH molecule contains 6 H atoms, so 1 mol contains 6 × 6.02 × 1023 = 3.6 × 1024 H atoms. 6 is the number per molecule, not per mole.
Divide by Ar: C 72/12 = 6, H 12/1 = 12, O 16/16 = 1, giving C6H12O. The C : H ratio is 6 : 12 = 1 : 2.
n = c × V: A 0.0050, B 0.0080, C 0.0300 × 0.300 = 0.0090, D 0.0080 mol. C contains the most solute.
Each CO2 has 2 O atoms: n(O) = 0.0500 × 2 = 0.100 mol; atoms = 0.100 × 6.02 × 1023 = 6.02 × 1022. A counts molecules, not O atoms.
Propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol are both C3H8O: 3(12) + 8(1) + 16 = 60. Propylamine, C3H9N, has Mr = 36 + 9 + 14 = 59.
n(H+) = c × V × (H+ per acid): A 0.020 × 2 × 2 = 0.080 mol; B 0.010 × 4 = 0.040; C 0.080 × 0.5 = 0.040; D 0.040 × 0.5 × 2 = 0.040. Remember H2SO4 releases two H+.
Molar mass has units of g mol<sup>−1</sup>. Relative atomic and molecular masses are ratios compared with 1/12 of a <sup>12</sup>C atom, and mass number is a count of nucleons, so they have no units.
n(NaOH) = 4 g ÷ 40 g mol⁻¹ = 0.1 mol. c = 0.1 mol ÷ 0.500 dm³ = 0.2 mol dm⁻³. Remember to convert 500 cm³ to 0.500 dm³.
1.5 mol CO2 contains 1.5 mol C; 2.0 mol H2O contains 4.0 mol H. C : H = 1.5 : 4.0 = 3 : 8, so the formula is C3H8 (already saturated, so molecular = empirical).
n = mass ÷ molar mass (g ÷ g mol⁻¹ = mol). For example, 18 g of water ÷ 18 g mol⁻¹ = 1 mol.
Each CH3COCH3 (C3H6O) has 10 atoms. Atoms = 0.20 × 10 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 1.2 × 10²⁴. Option A counts molecules, not atoms.
n(H2O) = 9.0 g ÷ 18 g mol⁻¹ = 0.50 mol. Molecules = 0.50 × 6.02 × 10²³ = 3.0 × 10²³. A gives the amount in moles, not the number of molecules.
n(CO2) = 88 g ÷ 44 g mol⁻¹ = 2.0 mol. Each CO2 has 3 atoms, so amount of atoms = 2.0 × 3 = 6 mol. A and B are numbers of particles, not amounts in moles.
Number of molecules = n × NA = 2.0 × 10−21 mol × 6.02 × 1023 mol−1 ≈ 1.2 × 103. A is just the amount in moles, not the number of particles.
n(NaOH) = 0.050 dm3 × 0.10 mol dm−3 = 5.0 × 10−3 mol. Each NaOH gives two ions (Na+ and OH−), so ions = 1.0 × 10−2 mol. B forgets that there are two ions per formula unit.
Each KAl(SO4)2 gives 2 SO42−, so 0.40 mol sulfate in 0.100 dm3: [SO42−] = 0.40/0.100 = 4.0 mol dm−3. C forgets the factor of 2.
M = MgSO4 + 7H2O = (24.3 + 32.1 + 64.0) + 7 × 18.0 = 120.4 + 126 ≈ 246 g mol−1. A is the anhydrous salt only; the water of crystallization must be included.
C5H12 cannot be simplified (5 and 12 have no common factor), so its empirical and molecular formulas are the same. C5H10 and C4H8 reduce to CH2, and C4H10 reduces to C2H5. A.
M(C2H6) = 30 g mol−1. Mass of one molecule = 30 g / 6.02 × 1023 = 5.0 × 10−23 g. C is the mass of one mole, not one molecule.
Avogadro's law: at constant P and T, equal volumes of gases contain equal numbers of particles, so V ∝ n, i.e. V/n = constant. A is the pressure law and B is Charles's law.
Moles: C 12/12 = 1, H 2/1 = 2, O 16/16 = 1, so the empirical formula is CH2O (M = 30). 60/30 = 2, so the molecular formula is C2H4O2.
n(NaCl) = 0.200 dm3 × 0.5 mol dm−3 = 0.10 mol. New volume = 200 + 300 = 500 cm3, so c = 0.10/0.500 = 0.2 mol dm−3. Using 300 cm3 as the final volume gives the wrong answer D.
The CH2 unit has M = 14; 56 ÷ 14 = 4, so the molecular formula is (CH2)4 = C4H8.
Each C6H5CONH2 molecule has 5 + 2 = 7 H atoms. Number of H atoms = 7 × 1.0 mol × 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹ = 4.2 × 10²⁴. Option A gives atoms per molecule, not per mole.
Each CuSO4•5H2O contains 4 + 5 = 9 O atoms. O atoms = 0.100 mol × 9 × 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹ = 5.42 × 10²³. Counting only the 4 sulfate O atoms would give 2.41 × 10²³ (C).

By Avogadro's law, identical containers at the same conditions hold the same number of moles, so the gas with the largest molar mass has the highest mass: O<sub>2</sub> (32) > C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub> (30) > N<sub>2</sub> (28) > Ne (20).
n(FeSO4) = 0.100 dm³ × 0.020 mol dm⁻³ = 2.0 × 10⁻³ mol, and each FeSO4 gives one SO42−, so 2.0 × 10⁻³ mol.
Each CH3OH molecule contains 4 H atoms. H atoms = 0.500 mol × 4 × 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹ = 1.20 × 10²⁴.
Each [Pt(NH3)2Cl2] unit has 1 Pt + 2 × 4 (NH3) + 2 Cl = 11 atoms. Atoms = 0.100 mol × 11 × 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹ = 6.62 × 10²³. A (11) is atoms per formula unit.
n(O2) = 3.20 g ÷ 32.00 g mol⁻¹ = 0.100 mol. At 273 K and 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa, V = 0.100 mol × 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹ = 2.24 dm³. B (4.48) wrongly uses M = 16 for O2.

Each (NH<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>4</sub> contains 3 NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> + 1 PO<sub>4</sub><sup>3−</sup> = 4 ions. Number of ions = 0.20 × 4 × 6.02 × 10<sup>23</sup> = 4.8 × 10<sup>23</sup>. B counts formula units only.
PtCl<sub>2</sub>(NH<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub> has 1 Pt + 2 Cl + 2 × (1 N + 3 H) = 11 atoms. Number of atoms = 0.10 × 11 × 6.02 × 10<sup>23</sup> = 6.6 × 10<sup>23</sup>.
Each glucose molecule contains 6 O atoms. Number of O atoms = 0.200 mol × 6 × 6.02 × 10<sup>23</sup> mol<sup>−1</sup> = 7.22 × 10<sup>23</sup>. A gives the amount in mol, not the number of atoms.

Dioxin (dibenzo-p-dioxin) has two benzene rings (12 C, 8 H) joined by two O atoms: C<sub>12</sub>H<sub>8</sub>O<sub>2</sub>. Dividing by 2 gives the empirical formula C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>4</sub>O. D is the molecular formula, not the simplest ratio.
Each formula unit contains 2 NH4+ ions, so n(NH4+) = 2 × 0.040 = 0.080 mol. Concentration = 0.080 mol ÷ 0.200 dm3 = 0.40 mol dm−3. 0.20 forgets the factor of 2.

Benzene, C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>6</sub>, has the lowest H : C ratio (1 : 1), so the highest % carbon: 72.06/78.12 = 92.3%. Compare CH<sub>4</sub> 74.9%, C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>4</sub> 85.6%, C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub> 82.7%.
n(Cl−): A 0.020 × 0.50 = 0.010; B 0.060 × 0.20 × 2 = 0.024; C 0.070 × 0.30 = 0.021 mol. In D the Cl is covalently bonded in ClCH2COOH, so it gives no chloride ions.
Each H2 molecule has 2 protons and 2 electrons, so 4 particles per molecule. For one mole: 4 × 6.02 × 1023 = 2.4 × 1024. 1.2 × 1024 counts only protons or only electrons.

C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>5</sub>OH (C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>6</sub>O) cannot be simplified, so its empirical and molecular formulas are the same. CH<sub>3</sub>COOH → CH<sub>2</sub>O, C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>6</sub> → CH and C<sub>8</sub>H<sub>18</sub> → C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>9</sub> all reduce.
At the same T and p, volume ratio = mole ratio. X : CO2 : H2O = 15 : 60 : 75 = 1 : 4 : 5, so each molecule has 4 C atoms and 10 H atoms: C4H10.
%N = mass of N ÷ Mr: N2H4 = 28.02 ÷ 32.06 = 87%; NH3 = 82%; N2O4 = 30%; NaNO3 = 16%. Hydrazine has the most N per unit mass.
Each (NH4)2CO3 contains 2 N atoms, so n(N) = 2 × 0.50 = 1.0 mol. Number of atoms = 1.0 × 6.02 × 1023 = 6.02 × 1023.
Ratio C : H : O = 58.8/12.0 : 9.80/1.0 : 31/16.0 = 4.9 : 9.8 : 1.94 ≈ 5 : 10 : 2, so the empirical formula C5H10O2 has Mr = 102, the same as the molecular mass: C5H10O2.
C : H = 84.6/12.01 : 15.4/1.01 = 7.04 : 15.2 ≈ 5 : 11, so the empirical formula is C5H11 (M = 71.2). 142.3 ÷ 71.2 = 2, so the molecular formula is C10H22.

Each formula unit of Na2CO3•10H2O contains 3 + 10 = 13 O atoms. n(O) = 2.0 × 13 = 26 mol; number of atoms = 26 × 6.02 × 1023 = 1.6 × 1025. Option B (26) is the amount in moles, not the number of atoms.
n(Na2SO4) = 1.42 ÷ 142 = 0.0100 mol. Dilution does not change the moles, so V = 0.0100 ÷ 0.020 = 0.500 dm3 = 500 cm3 (the total volume, not the volume of water added).
n(NaHCO3) = 0.50/84 mol, and each NaHCO3 gives one HCO3−. c = n ÷ V(dm3) = 0.50 ÷ (84 × 0.250) mol dm−3. The volume must be in dm3, not cm3 (D).
Moles: C = 75/12 = 6.25; H = 25/1 = 25. Ratio C : H = 6.25 : 25 = 1 : 4, so the empirical formula is CH4.
Moles of O atoms: A, Mg(NO3)2 has 6 O: 0.05 × 6 = 0.30. B, C6H4(NO2)2 has 4 O: 0.20. C, H2O: 0.10. D, NO2: 0.20. A has the most.
n = c × V = 0.10 mol dm−3 × 0.250 dm3 = 0.025 mol. Remember to convert 250 cm3 to dm3.
n(Cl−) = (0.200 × 1) + (0.200 × 5) = 1.2 mol in a total of 0.400 dm3, so [Cl−] = 1.2/0.400 = 3 mol dm−3.
44 g CO2 = 1 mol C (12 g); 18 g H2O = 2 mol H (2 g). Oxygen = 30 − 12 − 2 = 16 g = 1 mol O. Ratio C : H : O = 1 : 2 : 1 → CH2O.
M(C60) = 60 × 12 = 720 g mol−1; mass of one molecule = 720/(6.0 × 1023) = 1.2 × 10−21 g.

10 cm<sup>3</sup> of A is left, so 10 cm<sup>3</sup> A reacts with 20 cm<sup>3</sup> B to give 10 cm<sup>3</sup> product. By Avogadro's law the mole ratio A : B : product = 1 : 2 : 1, so the product is AB<sub>2</sub> (x = 1, y = 2).

Soot (carbon from a yellow, incomplete-combustion flame) deposited on the crucible adds mass every time, a systematic error in the mass of oxide. The lid being slightly ajar is correct technique (lets O<sub>2</sub> in) and white powder is the expected MgO.
